=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- tests/inventory_parity.py:55 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: EXAMPLE_PREFIX_RE = re.compile(r"(?:such as|for example|e\.g\.)\s*$", re.IGNORECASE) uses a `$` anchor that only matches when the example phrase is the last thing before the code span on the line.
  WHY: common prose like "For example, see `scripts/foo.py`" or "such as, `prompts/mode-bar.txt`" will not be recognized as examples and can trigger false-positive inventory failures.
- tests/inventory_parity.py:119-139 | severity=nit | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: parse_secondary_document calls `document_path.read_text()` without handling FileNotFoundError.
  WHY: if README.md or agents.md is renamed or deleted, the gate crashes with a traceback instead of emitting the structured FAIL message the rest of the parity gate uses.
- Requirement: "Extend the inventory parity gate so it audits the documentation surfaces named in the plan: README.md, agents.md, and docs/INVENTORY.md" (linked issue #3371 item 1)
  Expected change site: tests/inventory_parity.py — parse_secondary_document
  Evidence of absence: parse_secondary_document only extracts tracked-surface references from list-item lines (matching LIST_LINE_RE) and table rows (matching TABLE_LINE_RE), plus the `path=` assignment scan. Code-span references on ordinary prose lines are discarded. Empirical scan: README.md has 37 unique tracked-surface references on prose lines (though most are `ai-*` wrapper names filtered by `is_generated_wrapper_reference`); agents.md has 8 unique tracked-surface references on prose lines (e.g., `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py`, `scripts/write_codex_config.sh`, `scripts/run_workspace_hook.sh`). These prose references are never validated against INVENTORY.md. The implementation audits a structural subset (list/table lines) rather than the full documented surfaces.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  WHY: files in subdirectories under "scripts" or other top-level directories would be misclassified as None and could escape inventory parity enforcement.

  WHY: many legitimate tracked-surface references in README.md/agents.md appear in prose paragraphs but are never validated, so the gate only audits a structural subset rather than the full documentation surfaces.

  Expected change site: tests/inventory_parity.py — mainly parse_secondary_document function coverage
  Evidence of absence: The docstring mentions the added surfaces and README.md/agents.md tables are added, but parse_secondary_document only parses tracked paths from README.md and agents.md when they appear on list-item or table-formatted lines and only scans list/table structure / literal path= assignments.
